title: Dataverse semantic model: what do agents know about your business data, and who tunes it?
summary: The documented behavior, costs, permissions and controls are supported by Microsoft documentation. Minor corrections should complete the signal-setting route and acknowledge Microsoft's differing labels for the app-level Copilot setting.

claims.claim: The Dataverse semantic model gives agents and Copilot shared business context beyond raw table and column names.
claims.quote: The Dataverse semantic model gives AI agents and Copilot experiences a shared, business-aware understanding of your Dataverse data. Rather than reasoning from raw column and table names alone, agents that consume the semantic model understand what your data means.

claims.claim: The platform automatically provisions models for supported Copilot experiences.
claims.quote: The platform automatically provisions semantic models for supported Copilot experiences over Dataverse data.

claims.where: summary; What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Makers and administrators can tune table sources, signals and glossary terms.
claims.quote: Makers and administrators can then fine-tune each model's table sources and signals, and add domain-specific glossary terms for business language that automatic extraction can't infer.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risks and limits: Not an access control
claims.claim: Model table and signal configuration does not replace Dataverse security roles or table, column and record access controls.
claims.quote: They don't override or replace Dataverse security roles, table-, column-, or record-level access controls, or application-level configurations.

claims.where: What it is: Three building blocks
claims.claim: Data scope defines the Dataverse tables covered, with semantic indexing over those tables.
claims.quote: The data scope defines the set of Dataverse tables covered by the semantic model. Semantic indexing is applied over those tables

claims.where: What it is: Three building blocks
claims.claim: System-inferred signals include table relationships.
claims.quote: Table relationships | How records across tables are associated, such as one-to-many and many-to-many relationships.

claims.where: What it is: Three building blocks
claims.claim: View signals include public views with join conditions and sub-grid views.
claims.quote: Views | Public views with join conditions and sub-grid views that define which records and columns are relevant for a scenario.

claims.where: What it is: Three building blocks
claims.claim: System-inferred signals include form summaries.
claims.quote: Forms summaries | Context summarized from forms and form fields.

claims.where: What it is: Three building blocks
claims.claim: System-inferred signals include table summaries.
claims.quote: Table summaries | Context generated from table descriptions, column headers, and column descriptions.

claims.where: What it is: Three building blocks
claims.claim: Sample data rows are an optional signal.
claims.quote: The semantic model automatically extracts signals from metadata that already exists in your Dataverse environment: table and column descriptions, table relationships, views, forms, and optionally sample data rows.

claims.where: What it is: Three building blocks
claims.claim: The glossary holds business terms, acronyms and definitions that system signals cannot infer.
claims.quote: The glossary allows makers to add domain-specific terms, acronyms, synonyms, and definitions that system signals can't infer.

claims.claim: Enabling Dataverse intelligence automatically provisions the semantic model.
claims.quote: Once Dataverse intelligence is enabled, the semantic model is provisioned automatically.

claims.claim: The model regenerates automatically every 12 hours.
claims.quote: The semantic model regenerates automatically every 12 hours to reflect schema changes.

claims.claim: Initial generation can take up to two hours.
claims.quote: Initial generation can take up to two hours

claims.claim: Dataverse intelligence is now part of Business Applications in Work IQ.
claims.quote: Dataverse intelligence is now part of Business Applications in Work IQ.

claims.claim: Copilot in Power Apps consumes the semantic model over Dataverse data.
claims.quote:
The semantic model is automatically consumed by the following experiences:
- Copilot in Power Apps

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot with Dataverse consumes the semantic model.
claims.quote: The semantic model is automatically consumed by the following experiences: ... Microsoft Copilot with Dataverse

claims.claim: Sales Agent in Microsoft 365 consumes the semantic model.
claims.quote: The semantic model is automatically provisioned and consumed by the following Copilot and agent experiences when they are set up over Dataverse data: ... Sales Agent in Microsoft 365

claims.claim: Copilot Studio agents over Dataverse data consume the semantic model.
claims.quote: The semantic model is automatically provisioned and consumed by the following Copilot and agent experiences when they are set up over Dataverse data: ... Microsoft Copilot Studio agents over Dataverse data

claims.claim: A model's name reflects the source that provisioned it.
claims.quote: Semantic models are named based on the source that provisioned them.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits: Shared models change together
claims.claim: Changes to a shared model's signals, tables and glossary affect every associated app or agent, including the SalesSpecificQnA example.
claims.quote: If multiple apps or agents share the same semantic model (for example, Sales Agent and Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales both use SalesSpecificQnA), changes to that model apply to all experiences associated with it.

claims.claim: A custom semantic model can be created for a specific purpose.
claims.quote: You can also create a custom model for a specific purpose.

claims.claim: Custom models are currently usable through direct API and action calls.
claims.quote: Custom models are currently usable through direct API and action calls

claims.claim: Creating a custom model does not automatically connect it to an app or agent.
claims.quote: Creating one doesn't automatically connect it to an app or agent.

claims.where: What it is: Custom models; controls[1].note
claims.claim: Custom model creation is preview.
claims.quote: Create a custom semantic model (preview)

claims.where: What it is: The other meaning
claims.claim: Power BI semantic models in Fabric logically describe an analytical domain using metrics and business-friendly terminology.
claims.quote: In Microsoft Fabric, Power BI semantic models are a logical description of an analytical domain, with metrics, business friendly terminology, and representation, to enable deeper analysis.

claims.where: What it is: The other meaning
claims.claim: Fabric and Power BI semantic models are separate analytical objects managed in Fabric and Power BI rather than the Dataverse configuration described here.
claims.quote: Semantic models are independent items in Fabric and can be managed via REST APIs to enumerate semantic models in a workspace

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments created for new or existing tenants.

claims.claim: Environments provisioned in the EU and EFTA are exceptions to that default.
claims.quote: European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned in the EU and EFTA macro region geography.

claims.claim: Government-related environments are exceptions to that default.
claims.quote: Government-related environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned by customers with current or previous government cloud deployments that are likely to depend on FedRAMP security controls.

claims.claim: Nonproduction environments are exceptions to that default.
claims.quote: Nonproduction environments: This exception applies to trial, sandbox, and developer environments.

claims.claim: Semantic modeling is one of the capabilities available with Work IQ.
claims.quote: When Work IQ is on, a new environment can use the following capabilities: ... Semantic modeling.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a licence requirement specific to the semantic model, distinct from the consuming experience.
claims.quote: Searched: "semantic model" "license" Dataverse pricing; read semantic-model-overview, fine-tune-semantic-model-signals, semantic-model-faq, Work IQ understand-costs, Ask API licensing and Work IQ API overview. Requirements follow the experience/API; no separate model licence found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a price specific to the semantic model.
claims.quote: Searched: "semantic model" "license" Dataverse pricing; Dataverse semantic model licensing pricing audit events. Read model overview, configuration, FAQ, Work IQ understand-costs and API licensing. Storage and consuming-experience charges are documented, not a separate model price.

claims.claim: Semantic modeling is among the Work IQ features that use extra storage for search indexes.
claims.quote: Some features use extra storage for search indexes. These features include semantic modeling and access to Power Apps and Dynamics 365 data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: All Dataverse indexes are reported at the Dataverse database capacity rate.
claims.quote: All Dataverse indexes are reported at the Dataverse database capacity rate.

claims.claim: Search storage is reported at environment level as DataverseSearch in the capacity report.
claims.quote: Storage consumed by Dataverse search is reported at the environment level as a table called DataverseSearch.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ billing follows the experience consuming the business context.
claims.quote: For Business Applications in Work IQ, you track cost by the experiences people use rather than by a dedicated business applications category.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises configuring the spending policy for the consuming experience.
claims.quote: Configure the policy for the consuming experience rather than looking for a separate business applications spending policy.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Not an access control
claims.claim: Removing a table from a model does not delete the Dataverse table.
claims.quote: Removing a table from the model doesn't delete the Dataverse table.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not instant; controls[4].note
claims.claim: Saving model configuration and regenerating the model are separate steps.
claims.quote: Saving configuration and regenerating the model are separate operations.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not instant; controls[4].note
claims.claim: Unsaved edits are not included in regeneration, so changes should be saved first.
claims.quote: Save changes before selecting Regenerate. Unsaved edits aren't included in the request.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not instant
claims.claim: A regeneration-started message indicates acceptance rather than completion.
claims.quote: A message that regeneration started successfully confirms that the request was accepted, not that generation has completed.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not instant; controls[4].note
claims.claim: Regeneration runs across all semantic models in the environment.
claims.quote: Regeneration runs across all semantic models in the environment.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Generated content is read-only
claims.claim: Generated summaries, views and relationships cannot be edited directly.
claims.quote: Generated summaries, views, and relationships are read-only.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Sample data rows add row values; controls[2].note
claims.claim: Sample table rows is off by default.
claims.quote: The Sample table rows signal is turned off by default.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Sample data rows add row values
claims.claim: Enabling Sample table rows uses selected row values as agent context.
claims.quote: When available and enabled, it uses a selection of row values to give agents context about the table's content.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Environment copy or move
claims.claim: The overview says semantic models do not support environment copy or move operations.
claims.quote: The semantic model currently doesn't support environment copy or move operations.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Environment copy or move
claims.claim: The overview advises restarting Dataverse Intelligence after an environment copy or move.
claims.quote: After any environment copy or move, turn Dataverse Intelligence off and back on in the Power Platform Admin Center to force a restart.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Environment copy or move
claims.claim: The configuration article says semantic model configuration is solution-aware and can move between environments in solutions.
claims.quote: Semantic models are solution-aware, which means you can package them into solutions for application lifecycle management (ALM). This capability allows you to move semantic model configuration between environments as part of your deployment process.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Environment copy or move
claims.claim: Models with Secondary_model in their name do not carry over in environment copy or move operations.
claims.quote: Secondary_model is a naming convention that indicates the semantic model isn't ALM-compatible. If you see this term in a model name, the model doesn't carry over when you copy or move the environment.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is unavailable in sovereign or government clouds, including DoD, GCC and GCC High.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ isn't currently available in sovereign or government cloud environments, including Department of Defense (DoD), Government Community Cloud (GCC), and GCC High.

claims.claim: Power Apps > environment > More > Discover all > AI > Semantic models reaches the environment's model inventory and associated apps or agents.
claims.quote: select More, and if not in the More list, select Discover all, and then select Semantic models under AI section.

claims.claim: GET [Organization URI]/api/iq/v1.0/semanticmodel lists models in the current environment.
claims.quote:
The List operation returns semantic models available in the current Dataverse environment.
GET [Organization URI]/api/iq/v1.0/semanticmodel HTTP/1.1

claims.claim: The include=botinfo query parameter identifies apps and agents using each model.
claims.quote: Use the optional include=botinfo query parameter to identify app modules, bot components, and agents that use each semantic model.

claims.claim: The Power Apps model route through Configure > Configure table sources > Included in model > table > Remove table removes a table from model scope.
claims.quote: Open the model and select Configure. Under Configure table sources, select All tables to find an available table, or Included in model to review the current selection. Search for the table display name and select the table. Select Add table or Remove table, as appropriate.

claims.claim: POST [Organization URI]/api/iq/v1.0/semanticmodel creates a custom model associated with selected tables, as qualified in the note.
claims.quote:
The create operation associates a unique name with one or more Dataverse tables.
POST [Organization URI]/api/iq/v1.0/semanticmodel HTTP/1.1

claims.claim: The create-model request body names tables in its tables property.
claims.quote: tables | Array of String | Yes | One or more Dataverse table logical names to associate with the model.

claims.claim: The Power Apps model route through Configure > Manage signals reaches model-wide signal settings.
claims.quote: Open the model and select Configure. Under Manage signals, turn the relevant signal On or Off.
claims.fix: Complete controls[2].ui.path and its rendered counterpart as 'environment > More > Discover all > AI > Semantic models > model > Configure > Manage signals > signal > On or Off'. Keep the existing note that per-table, view and relationship controls are on Configure.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls: What they do not enforce
claims.claim: No API or PowerShell operation is documented for setting model signal types, views or relationships.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse semantic model signals regeneration API PowerShell dvtablesearch; "Dataverse" "semantic" "signals" "API" configuration. Read Ask manage-semantic-models, configuration, dvtablesearch and dvtablesearchentity references; no documented signal-setting operation or schema.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risks and limits: Generated content is read-only
claims.claim: The Configure page also contains per-table signal and individual view or relationship toggles.
claims.quote: Open the model, select Configure, and select an included table. Open Views or Relationships to review the generated items.

claims.claim: Power Apps > environment > More > Discover all > AI > Semantic models > model > Glossary > Add term reaches glossary creation.
claims.quote: Open the semantic models page and select the model you want to update. Select Glossary. In the new semantic model experience, you can also select Go to Glossary on Overview. ... In Glossary, select Add term.

claims.claim: POST [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/copilotglossaryterms creates a glossary term.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/copilotglossaryterms ... Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE

claims.claim: The glossary term entity supports POST, GET, PATCH and DELETE.
claims.quote: Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE

claims.claim: The glossary request uses term for the term and description for its explanation.
claims.quote: description | Edm.String | Explanation of the term. ... term | Edm.String | Display name: Term

claims.claim: System-defined glossary terms and definitions can be edited.
claims.quote: You can't delete system-defined glossary entries, but you can edit them to update the term or definition.

claims.claim: System-defined glossary entries cannot be deleted.
claims.quote: The Delete action is disabled for system-defined entries.

claims.claim: The Power Apps model route ending in model > Regenerate requests manual regeneration.
claims.quote: Open the model you want to review from the semantic models page in Power Apps. ... Select Regenerate in the model's command bar.

claims.where: controls[4].api; Governance controls: What they do not enforce
claims.claim: No API or PowerShell operation is documented for semantic model regeneration.
claims.quote: Searched: "semantic model" "regenerate" "API" Dataverse; Dataverse semantic model signals regeneration API PowerShell dvtablesearch. Read regeneration, Ask manage-semantic-models and dvtablesearch operation reference; no regeneration API or cmdlet found.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Manage > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ controls environment Work IQ features.
claims.quote: select Manage. Select the environment that you want to manage. On the command bar, select Settings. Select Product > Features. Find Work IQ, and then turn the setting on or off.

claims.where: controls[5].api; Governance controls: What they do not enforce
claims.claim: No API or PowerShell equivalent is documented for the environment Work IQ switch.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ environment tenant setting API PowerShell Business Applications data available Copilot; "Work IQ" "Power Platform API" settings; "Work IQ" "Set-Organization". Read default-settings, manage-participation and returned settings-features excerpt; no matching operation found.

claims.claim: The environment Work IQ setting requires an environment administrator account.
claims.quote: You need an environment administrator account.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot controls the tenant audience.
claims.quote: In the left navigation pane, select Copilot > Settings. In Copilot settings, select View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.

claims.where: controls[6].api; Governance controls: What they do not enforce
claims.claim: No API or PowerShell operation is documented for the tenant Business Applications data in Work IQ audience switch.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ environment tenant setting API PowerShell Business Applications data available Copilot; "Business Applications" "Copilot" "Graph" tenant settings. Read default-settings and returned Graph TCM/Copilot resources excerpts; no operation for this switch found.

claims.claim: The tenant audience options are No users, All users and Specific groups.
claims.quote: To turn off access for everyone, select No users. To turn on access for everyone, select All users. ... To provide access to a limited audience, select Specific groups

claims.claim: All users is the default tenant audience.
claims.quote: To turn on access for everyone, select All users. This option is the default.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center setting requires a tenant administrator account.
claims.quote: You need a tenant administrator account.

claims.claim: Power Apps > Apps > app > Edit > Settings > Features > Enable Microsoft 365 Copilot in model-driven apps controls app participation.
claims.quote: select Apps. Find the app that you want to manage, and then select Edit. ... select Settings. Select Features. Set Enable Microsoft 365 Copilot in model-driven apps to On or Off.
claims.fix: Keep the cited route, but add to controls[7].note and the rendered note: 'The model-driven app setup article labels this option Microsoft Copilot in model-driven apps; the Work IQ default-settings article calls it Enable Microsoft 365 Copilot in model-driven apps.' Both pages are already cited: https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/model-driven-apps/add-microsoft-365-copilot and https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/business-applications-work-iq/default-settings.

claims.claim: POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/SaveSettingValue creates or updates an app-level setting override.
claims.quote: SaveSettingValue Action ... Creates or updates app/organization level override.

claims.claim: The app's Copilot setting identifier supplied as SettingName is m365copilotmodelappenabled.
claims.quote: For the model-driven app, the Enable M365 Copilot in model-driven apps setting (m365copilotmodelappenabled) must be set to Default or On.

claims.claim: SaveSettingValue uses Value to supply the setting override.
claims.quote: Value | Edm.String | False | False | Overridden value that needs to be set (Required).

claims.claim: SaveSettingValue uses AppUniqueName to target a model-driven app.
claims.quote: AppUniqueName | Edm.String | True | False | Model-driven app unique name (Optional).

claims.claim: The app-level participation setting requires a maker account.
claims.quote: You need a maker account.

claims.claim: The app must be saved and published after changing its Copilot setting.
claims.quote: Select Save. Select Publish.

claims.claim: Managing a model requires System Administrator or the combination of Dataverse Search, Semantic Model and Environment Maker.
claims.quote: You need either of the following security roles to manage the semantic model: System Administrator -or- Dataverse Search, Semantic Model and Environment Maker.

claims.claim: Power Platform administrators manage Work IQ participation settings.
claims.quote: Power Platform Administrator role to manage settings and assign other roles.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Work IQ settings cascade through tenant, environment and app levels.
claims.quote: You manage Business Applications in Work IQ through a cascading set of settings at three levels:

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Turning off the tenant setting stops sharing between Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Dataverse even when an app is configured to share.
claims.quote: If you turn off this setting, data isn't shared between Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Dataverse, even if an app is configured to share data.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Turning off the environment Work IQ setting makes semantic modeling unavailable there.
claims.quote: The Work IQ setting turns on business skills, semantic modeling, and access to Dataverse data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Research, and Agent Builder. If you turn off this setting, these features aren't available in the environment.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: A model-wide signal setting takes precedence over per-table signal settings.
claims.quote: A model-wide signal setting takes precedence over per-table settings.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: The corresponding signal must be enabled at model and table levels to manage individual views or relationships.
claims.quote: To manage individual views or relationships, the corresponding signal must be enabled at both levels.

claims.claim: The Configure interface requires the new semantic model experience.
claims.quote: Custom model creation and the Configure interface are available only in environments where the new semantic model experience is enabled and its version requirements are met.

claims.where: Governance controls: New experience; Open questions
claims.claim: New-experience availability depends on environment enablement and Dataverse and installed solution versions.
claims.quote: The experience also depends on the environment's Dataverse and installed solution versions and whether it's enabled for that environment.

claims.where: Governance controls: What they do not enforce
claims.claim: Work IQ participation settings do not prevent agentic access to environment data.
claims.quote: These participation settings don't prevent agentic access to environment data.

claims.where: Governance controls: What they do not enforce
claims.claim: Microsoft points to App Access controls to manage agentic access to environment data.
claims.quote: Use App Access controls to manage that access.

claims.claim: The semantic model articles do not list audit events for changes to model tables, signals or glossary.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dataverse" "semantic model" "audit"; Dataverse semantic model licensing pricing audit events. Read overview, configuration, FAQ, glossary, regeneration and API references; no named model-change events. General Dataverse auditing results do not supply those event names.
